setup.title: Hushpad — Vault folder and passphrase
setup.intro1: All notes are saved in this one folder as encrypted files. Other apps and people can open the files but can’t read them.
setup.intro2: To use it on several computers, pick a folder inside a synced folder such as Dropbox or OneDrive, then choose the same folder and passphrase on the other computers.
setup.intro2@mac: To use it on several computers, pick a folder inside a synced folder such as Dropbox or iCloud Drive, then choose the same folder and passphrase on the other computers.
setup.intro3: On this computer you enter the passphrase only once. It’s remembered for your Windows account, so you won’t be asked again.
setup.intro3@mac: On this Mac you enter the passphrase only once. It’s kept in your keychain, so you won’t be asked again.
setup.warn: ⚠ If you forget the passphrase, no one (not even the developer) can recover your notes. Write it down somewhere safe.
setup.existing: ✔ This folder already has Hushpad notes — enter its passphrase.
setup.new: A new vault folder will be created — choose a passphrase (8+ characters).
setup.not_empty: This folder isn’t empty. Create the Hushpad files in it anyway?
pwd.title: Change passphrase
pwd.note: Other computers will ask for the new passphrase once, the next time they open the vault.
pwd.invalid: Use at least 8 characters, and type the same passphrase twice.

imp.title: Import Windows Notepad tabs
imp.info: Copies the tabs open in Windows Notepad (including unsaved ones) into Hushpad. Notepad itself isn’t changed. Tabs you’ve already imported are unchecked.
imp.as_text: Import as code notes (recommended for HTML, JSON or code)

perm.msg@mac:
Hushpad needs screen recording permission for screenshots and screen recording.

Turn on Hushpad in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then restart Hushpad.

rv.title: Show for remote viewing
rv.body: When Hushpad shows as a black box over remote access (Chrome Remote Desktop, AnyDesk, TeamViewer…) or screen sharing, enter your passphrase to make it visible for a while. It hides again when the time is up or when you lock. Meanwhile other apps' screenshots and recordings can capture it too.
